title: Utility types
subtitle: Partial, Pick/Omit, union tools, ReturnType, Nest DTO derivation

cards.meaning: Built-in generic types that transform other types so you keep a single source of truth (entity/DTO) and derive variants instead of duplicating 15 fields by hand. Add a field to User and derived DTOs pick it up unless you omitted it. They are types only — mostly mapped and conditional under the hood.

cards.front: What does Partial<T> do, and is it deep?
cards.meaning: Makes all properties optional. Typical use: PATCH bodies and partial forms. It is shallow — nested objects are not deeply optional. A deep partial needs a custom mapped type.
cards.example: type UserPatch = Partial<User>; // { id?: string; name?: string }

cards.front: What do Required<T> and Readonly<T> do?
cards.meaning: Required makes all properties required (fully filled config). Readonly makes all properties readonly (immutable state shapes). Readonly is shallow and compile-time only — not Object.freeze, not deep immutability at runtime.

cards.front: What does Pick<T, K> do, and typical use?
cards.meaning: Keeps only keys K. Typical use: a short, explicit form subset of a DTO. K must be (or extend) keyof T.

cards.front: What does Omit<T, K> do, and when prefer it over Pick?
cards.meaning: Drops keys K — the practical “everything except…” transformer. Typical use: strip id / secrets. Prefer Omit for “entity minus server fields”; prefer Pick when the allowlist is short and explicit.

cards.front: What does Record<K, V> do, and why a literal-union K?
cards.meaning: An object type with keys K and values V. Typical use: dictionaries — Record<string, User>. When K is a literal union, keys become a required property set — good for exhaustive maps. Record<string, V> allows any string key and is weaker.

cards.front: What does Exclude<T, U> do, and typical use?
cards.meaning: Union minus members assignable to U (distributes over members). Typical use: strip a variant.

cards.front: What does Extract<T, U> do, and typical use?
cards.meaning: Union keeping members assignable to U. Typical use: pull a variant. Also used on object unions: Extract<Event, { type: 'click' }>.

cards.front: Exclude vs Omit — which works on what?
cards.meaning: Exclude filters unions (distributive). Omit drops object keys. Do not confuse union filtering with key dropping.
Removes null | undefined from T. Typical use: after a guard, or when modeling a required value. Equivalent idea: Exclude<T, null | undefined>.
cards.example: type U = NonNullable<string | null | undefined>; // string

cards.front: What does ReturnType<F> do, and the overload trap?
cards.meaning: The return type of function type F — derive from an existing function instead of duplicating the return interface. F must be a function type, often typeof someFn. Trap: on an overloaded function, ReturnType may pick an unexpected signature. Parameters<F> is the argument tuple for wrappers.

cards.front: What does Awaited<T> do, and how do you type fetchUser’s resolved value?
cards.meaning: Unwraps Promise, including nested promises. ReturnType of an async function is Promise<…>; Awaited<ReturnType<typeof fetchUser>> is the inner value so you do not duplicate the User shape.

cards.front: How do you derive response / create / PATCH DTOs from User?
cards.meaning: One entity, three projections. Response: Omit<User, 'passwordHash'>. Create: Omit<User, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'passwordHash'> & { password: string } — Omit drops secrets, & adds client-only fields. PATCH: Partial<Omit<User, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'passwordHash'>> — Omit locked keys, then Partial. New User fields flow in unless omitted.

cards.front: Can you call Partial(user) at runtime?
cards.meaning: No. Utilities are types only and erased. There is no Partial() runtime function from TypeScript. Nest still needs class-validator or Zod for runtime validation.

A mapped type: type Partial<T> = { [K in keyof T]?: T[K] }. Sketch only — it explains why Partial composes with keyof. Do not memorize Pick/Exclude definitions; they are the same idea (mapped vs distributive conditional).
cards.example: type Partial<T> = { [K in keyof T]?: T[K] };
